This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of M.V. Act,
claiming compensation on account of death of Muttappa Basappa Mannur, in the road accident dated 11.01.2024.
2.

The case of the petitioners, in brief, are as follows:
On 11.01.2024 at about 2.50 p.m., the deceased was riding the motorcycle bearing No. KA-51-HE-8579 wearing helmet slowly, cautiously and by observing all the traffic rules and norms at NH-44, Hosur to Bangalore Road

, when he reached near service road, Yadavanahalli Gate, the Tanker Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-T-7099 came in a high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle of the deceased from behind and caused the accident.
Due to the impact the deceased fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Sri.
Sai Hospital, Bangalore for treatment.
But he died in the hospital in-spite of best treatment given to him.
The deceased was hale and healthy, having robust health and strong personality.
He was aged about 36 years, working at Sandhar components factory and getting a salary of Rs.26,000/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.

Due to untimely death of deceased the petitioners have suffered mentally and physically,
they have lost their bread earner.

sentences.text:
The petitioners are claiming compensation under the heads of love and affection,
dependency, loss of estate, mental agony and shock, funeral expenses, medical expenses and consortium amounting to Rs.54,00,000/-.
The accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the tanker lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-T-7099.
In this regard, the case has been registered by Attibele Police in Crime No.14/2024.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.54,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices, respondent No.2 owner has not appeared before the court, hence placed as Exparte.

After service of summons, the respondent No.1 insurance company has appeared through its counsel and filed their written statement by denying the issuance of policy in respect of 2nd respondent to the Tanker Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-T-7099.

Further this respondent has denied the involvement of the offending vehicle and also contended that both the rider and driver of the offending lorry were not having valid driving license at the time of accident.
The compensation as claimed by the petitioners is excessive, exorbitant and fanciful.
Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

Further this respondent has denied the age,
avocation and income of the deceased.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contentions, the following issues were framed by this court:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that, they are the legal representatives and dependents of the deceased Sri. Muttappa Basappa Mannur?

2. Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Sri. Muttappa Basappa Mannur, had died due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident that occurred on 11.01.2024 at about 2.50 p.m. near service road, Yadavanahalli, NH-44 Hosur to Bengalore Road, Hejjal Wood Interior, Anekal Taluk, Bangalore, due to rash and negligent driving of driver of tanker lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-T-7099 as alleged?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as claimed?

If so, what amount and from whom?
4.
What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the first petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12.
Further the Assistant Manager at IDEAL WORKFORCE STAFFING SOLUTIONS PVT. LTD. is examined as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P13 to 17.

7. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2: In the affirmative,
 [
 Issue No.3: In the affirmative

8. The petitioners to prove their claim have produced true copies of FIR, complaint,
spot mahazar, spot sketch, IMV report, inquest report, PM report and charge sheet,
which are marked under Ex.P.1 to P7.
9.

As per the documents, produced by the petitioners, Ex.P1- FIR is came to be registered on the basis of first information given by the petitioner No.1 Smt. Netra.
10.
In the said Ex.P1, the first informant alleged the rash and negligent driving by the driver of tanker lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-T-7099.
The Ex.P2 & 3 are the spot mahazar and sketch.
As per the contents of Ex.P2 & 3 the accident spot is in the middle of the road.
As per the Ex.P4 IMV report the tanker lorry bearing Reg.No.TN- 52-T-7099 has got no visible damages but the motorcycle of petitioner has got severe damages.
It is alleged that the offending tanker lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-T-7099 came from Hosur side towards Bengaluru dashed against the rear side of the motorcycle of petitioner.
This shows the gross negligence by the driver of tanker lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-T-7099.

It is also established before this Tribunal that the driver of the tanker lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-T-7099 was not maintaining safe distance and was driving his Tanker in a rash and negligent manner and also was not in controllable speed as such, it dashed against the rear side of motorcycle of the petitioner.

Thereby,
the mahazar, rough sketch and IMV reports marked at Ex.P2, 3 & 4 prima-facie establishes the negligence on the part of driver of Tanker Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-T-7099.

sentences.text: Along with this if we perused the Ex.P5 inquest and Ex.P6 post mortem report it is evident that the death of deceased Sri. Muthappa Basappa Mannur was due to the complications of the injuries sustained by him at the time of accident.

12. Further the Ex.P7 charge sheet is filed against the driver of the Tanker Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-T- 7099 for the offences punishable U/Sec. 279 and 304(A) of IPC wherein the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of the the driver of the Tanker Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-T-7099.
No grounds are made out by the respondents to disbelieve the contents of charge sheet.

13. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.text: Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105,
where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105

In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities referred to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case on hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Tanker Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-T-7099 resulting in the death of one Sri Muthappa Basappa Mannur by sustaining injuries.
Wherefore Issue No.2 is answered in the Affirmative.

As held herein above, the petitioners have proved that Sri Muttappa Basappa Mannur died on 11.01.2024 due to the injuries sustained in RTA, which is caused by the driver of the Tanker Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-T-7099.

During the course of recording the evidence the notarized copies of Aadhaar cards are compared with the original documents and found correct.

18. In the absence of contradictory evidence the evidence of the petitioners is to be accepted and it is considered that, petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 & 3 are the minor children and petitioner No.4 is the mother of the deceased.

Accordingly, in this case the petitioner No.1 being the wife and petitioner No.2 & 3 being a minor children and petitioner No.4, being mother of deceased are entitled for the compensation in accordance with their dependency.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

The petitioners have produced D.L. of the deceased at Ex.P9.
As per the said document the deceased was born on 28.06.1987, the accident took place in the year-2024,
If it is considered, as on the date of the accident the age of the deceased was 37 years.
No other documents are produced by the petitioners to over come this contradictions.
Hence this court is accepting the age of the deceased as 37 years.

Thereby in the cases of income coming under the income tax limits the income tax has to be deducted and further the professional tax also should be deducted in the income of the deceased.
As per the brake up salary slip marked at Ex.P17 the gross monthly salary of the deceased was Rs.26,086/- in the month of November 2023.
In the said amount Rs.200/- has to be deducted towards professional tax, then the net income of the deceased for month was Rs.25,886/-.
As such the gross income of the deceased is taken at Rs.25,886/- x 12 = Rs.3,10,632/-.
The income of the deceased is established by the petitioners.
By applying the above said precedent, the income tax has to be deducted if the income of the deceased coming under the taxable income limits.
In the year 2024 the Tax rebate u/s 87A is available if the income is within Rs.5,00,000/-.
(Section 87A of Income Tax Act provides eligible taxpayers with a full income tax rebate if their total income is below Rs 5 lakh under the old tax regime.
Thereby as the annual income of the deceased was only Rs.3,10,632/- no income tax can be deducted.
25. As per Sarala varma's case the proper multiplier applicable to the age of deceased is 15.

Since there is four dependents on the deceased 1/4th of the income is to be deducted towards his personal expenses, then the total loss of dependency would be Rs.34,94,610/- (Rs.3,10,632/- X 15 =
Rs.46,59,480/- minus one fourth of the income i.e., (Rs.11,64,870/-) = Rs.34,94,610/-).

Liability:-
According to the petitioners the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1 in its objection statement has denied the issuance of policy to the Tanker Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-T-7099.
But has not lead any evidence by showing the dis entitlement of the petitioners.
The DL of the deceased also furnished by the petitioner, hence once again the defence of the respondent No.1 company is not acceptable.
In the charge sheet no offences are invoked by showing the non existence of the insurance policy to the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
The respondent No.1 insurance company has not lead any evidence in support of their defence.
In the absence of evidence any amount of pleadings is not helpful to consider the defence of the respondent.
Non existence of the policy is to be established by the respondent No.2 as per its pleading.
As such, the petitioners prima- facie established their case and the liability of respondent No.1 & 2.

Hence, the respondent No.1& 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.1 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.2.
The petitioners are entitled for the interest at 6% per annum.
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

31.

ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.50,23,454/-

from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The petitioners No.1 to 4 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 40:25:25:10:.
The respondent No.1 insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of awarded amount of petitioner No.1, 50% shall be released to petitioner No.1, on her proper identification and remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in her name in any Scheduled Bank,
